_readme: COPY THIS FOLDER, RENAME IT, EDIT THIS FILE. That is a haus.
2. change "id" to mynewhaus (lowercase, unique — it is how everything
refers to this haus, including your own material names below)
3. put the folder in user://hauses/ — on macOS:
5. start the game. Your banner is in the Hall.
Every field below except "id" is optional and degrades to a documented
default with a warning. The full guide, and the reasons behind the two
hard rules (the natural coat, and material roles): docs/HAUS-PACK.md
JSON has no comments, so the notes live in these "_" keys. The loader
ignores them; you can delete them.
name: Haus Yourhaus
_archetype: Picks the VOICE your haus taunts in (wolf, lion, stag, dragon, kraken,
rose, sun, falcon, trout, raven — or your own word, which falls back to a
generic proud-and-dangerous voice), and the mark tools/gen_sigils.gd draws
if you let it draw one.
_colors: Your heraldry. primary is the banner field, secondary and accent its
charges. They are also the ONLY colours your kit is allowed to wear —
the role gate checks every dressed surface against these four.
_tints: kit is THE JERSEY — the one saturated colour your tabards, cloaks, shield
faces, caparison, helm and crest are painted in. It can afford to be loud,
because since the material-role pass it is NOT painted on steel, leather,
skin, bone or the horse. piece and tower are the faint whisper natural
surfaces take so an army still hangs together; leave them out and they are
_coat: THE HARD RULE. Your horse is a horse: bay, dark_bay, chestnut,
liver_chestnut, black, white_grey, dapple_grey, drowned_grey, dun.
Pick one that stands off your jersey — a mount's haus identity is worn on
its caparison, not grown on the animal. (You may also declare your own
"coat_palette", but every colour in it must still be a colour a horse
comes in: near-colourless, or a warm brown.)
_art: Paths are relative to this folder (or absolute res:// / user://).
sigil      256x256 PNG with transparency — your shield. No sigil and the
Hall hangs a flat primary-colour shield instead.
will draw you one from the fields above.
pawn_helm  the footmen's half-helm. Name its two surfaces pawnhelm_iron
(the dome) and pawnhelm_accent (rim + motif) and the game paints
them for you. Keep it small: it WRAPS the skull.
crest      the knights'/queens'/kings' crest. Name the MESH NODE Crest_*
and it takes the jersey. This one TOWERS over the head.
Both are ordinary .glb files — they do not need importing.
hauses/_examples/ravenmark/make_props.gd builds a working pair of both in
~200 lines of GDScript if you have no modelling tool.
_materials: THE OTHER HARD RULE, and the reason this format exists.
The game paints your haus colour on KIT and on nothing else. Steel,
leather, wood, stone, skin, bone and the horse's coat are NATURAL and keep
their own colours; a crown is REGALIA and stays metal; a sigil or banner is
HERALDRY and carries its own artwork. Four rounds of art work went into
that rule, and a pack cannot undo it: you may only declare surfaces whose
names begin with "<your id>_", and a surface whose own name says steel,
leather, bone, hide or coat may not be declared kit.
Anything your models add BEYOND the contract names above must be declared
here, or the engine will refuse to paint it and the role gate will fail:
roles:  kit · natural:<stuff> · regalia · heraldry · effect
stuffs: steel leather wood stone skin bone coat glow atlas none
_extras: (types: pawn knight bishop queen king — there is no rook, the
rook is a watchtower flying your banner). If you override the
army you must declare at least one natural: a soldier made
